### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, touching **12** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-1.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **68** of **251** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **6** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b617675d2887f7b88e98a397011f70cf2004ae0c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `eb67a4efe2bb08afe037f7487a9d1a30ac5b3ae9` — the merge of head `1393d9772b7440f77ddae3158160dea7f33d0b09` into base `b617675d2887f7b88e98a397011f70cf2004ae0c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin eb67a4efe2bb08afe037f7487a9d1a30ac5b3ae9 && git checkout eb67a4efe2bb08afe037f7487a9d1a30ac5b3ae9
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b617675d2887f7b88e98a397011f70cf2004ae0c 1393d9772b7440f77ddae3158160dea7f33d0b09 && git checkout -B drift-repro b617675d2887f7b88e98a397011f70cf2004ae0c && git merge --no-ff 1393d9772b7440f77ddae3158160dea7f33d0b09

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b617675d2887f7b88e98a397011f70cf2004ae0c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b617675d2887f7b88e98a397011f70cf2004ae0c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

repo:objectstack#3 · os-support-ai · session_01WGufzi4PechTRCTBrfxV8W

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7cbaeefff2ed2e30bc6021c93228e0e87420a524`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/action-link-pages.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approvals-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/action-page-member.integration.test.ts + packages/spec/src/ui/action-params.zod.ts (`validateActionParams`, `isActionParamValuePresent`), packages/spec/src/contracts/approval-service.ts (`IApprovalService.handleActionPage` docblock), docs/adr/0043-actionable-approval-links.md, packages/runtime/src/domains/approvals.ts, packages/adapters/hono/src/index.ts (Response pass-through), packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/index.ts and package.json `exports`, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/sys-approval-action.object.ts — read, not reviewed. `.changeset/35722-action-link-reject-reason.md` and `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx` read for ② and agreement only.
Security-touching: yes
Rule-change-verified: none

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set, HTTP (the declared narrowing) — right.** `POST /api/v1/approvals/act` with a live reject token and a `comment` that is missing, blank, whitespace-only or not a string used to decide; it now answers `reason_required` (the confirm page again, `400`) and decides nothing. Both doors (the raw-app mount in `approvals-plugin.ts` and `handleActionPage`) get it from one builder, `actionRedemptionPage`.
- **Is it the only narrowing — no, there is a second population, and it is right but under-declared (S1).** `ApprovalService.redeemActionToken(token)` called in process on a reject token narrows the same way: the one-argument call that used to decide now returns `{ ok: false, reason: 'reason_required' }`. That is the intended behaviour; the changeset does not name it.
- **Exported types — they do move.** `ApprovalService` is exported from the package entry (`src/index.ts`), so its members are on the published type graph even though `ActionTokenOutcome` is not re-exported by name: (a) `redeemActionToken` gains an optional second parameter `input?: { comment?: unknown }` (additive; every old call still compiles); (b) `ActionTokenOutcome`, the return type of both `redeemActionToken` and `peekActionToken`, gains the arm `reason_required`. `renderConfirmPage` gains an optional `refusal`, and `actionRedemptionPage` / `REJECT_REASON_REQUIRED_COPY` are new module exports, but none of those three is addressable through `exports` — not published surface.
- **`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` — right.** No value any door refused before is accepted now; the new optional parameter only carries the reason the narrowed door demands. The direction is narrowing.
- **Approve — unchanged, right.** `rejecting` is read off the stored token row, never off the request; an approve reads no field, still records "Via action link", still consumes then decides. Pinned (`an approve reads no reason and keeps its fixed comment`).
- **Dead links, GET, 405 — unchanged, right.** `resolveActionToken` runs first, so a dead reject link with no reason is still told on the result page with `200` (pinned: the consumed reject token posted with `token` only). GET never decides.
- **`decide()` — unchanged.** `rejectReasonIssues` is a pure extraction of the same `validateActionParams` call.

### ② Semver level

- Level `patch` on `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` is right: AGENTS.md Post-Task 3 — the level follows `Metadata-protocol` alone, `none` takes `patch`, and "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition". `Metadata-protocol: none` is right (nothing an author writes moves). The `!` title, the BREAKING banner, FROM / TO, the one-line fix and exactly one ADR-0087 marker are all present; `Check Changeset` and the release gates are green on the head.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset, and agrees with ①.
- **S1 (should-fix) — the changeset under-declares what the diff publishes, and one sentence in it is false.** The ADR-0087 marker says "no export changes shape": the exported `ApprovalService` does — `redeemActionToken(rawToken, input?)` and the `reason_required` arm on the outcome both `redeemActionToken` and `peekActionToken` return. The BREAKING note and "the fix for a caller" address only the HTTP form; an in-process caller of `redeemActionToken(token)` on a reject token is broken the same way and its fix (`redeemActionToken(token, { comment })`, and handle `reason_required`) is not written. AGENTS.md requires a breaking changeset to carry its FROM / TO and one-line fix; this text ships as the package CHANGELOG, where earlier entries name `redeemActionToken` as a stable member. Fix on the prose face only (changeset; mirror in the PR body): correct the marker sentence, add the in-process FROM / TO and fix line. The disposition category itself (`not-required`, no stored row or authored value moves) holds.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty — nothing to answer.
- **Deviation: `400`, not `200`, for the blank-reason page — accepted.** The contract's "told on the page, never as an error status" (spec docblock, ADR-0043 Consequences) is about a dead link; this link is live and the input is what is refused, as on every other reject door (`400 VALIDATION_ERROR`). The body is still the HTML page; the hono adapter returns a `Response` from the dispatcher untouched, and the raw mount sets the status directly. Both doors are pinned byte-equal at `400`.
- **Deviation: static EN · 中文 copy instead of "every locale the package ships" — accepted.** The pages read no translation bundle and negotiate no locale by design (file header of `action-link-pages.ts`); the new label and refusal follow every other string on them. Per-locale copy would need a negotiation step these session-less pages deliberately lack — a separate card if wanted, not this one.
- **Deviation: no reviewer request sent — not a contract matter;** hand-over is the seat's.
- **Flag to the seat (landing, not contract):** the os-dev-report's `dogfood_battery` and the PR body's "Local runs" pin `a33c65f8`; the head is `7cbaeeff`, one later commit that only re-types `reqId` in `approval-service.test.ts`. The head's own check-runs are green (55 runs: success or skipped, none failed; `Dogfood Regression Gate` success). Whether the landing gate's head-pinned dogfood rule is met is the seat's L1 check.
- **SQL push-down:** no finding. The diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join; the one token lookup (`find` by `token_hash`, limit 1) is unchanged.
- PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]` — no off-relay write to name.

### ④ Design judgment

**The narrowing against the published spec.** It makes the platform's own refusal real: every other reject door already refuses a reject with no reason through the same judge, ADR-0043 lists comment capture on the confirm page as a v1 non-goal and "a fast follow", and the card carries the maintainer's requirement (#35593) that a rejection always has a reason. No declared capability is taken away beyond the canned-comment reject the card exists to remove.

Per file:

- **`approval-service.ts` — holds.** Order in `redeemActionToken`: resolve (dead link first) → reason judged → consume → decide. The refusal returns before the `sys_approval_token` update, with no await between the check and the consume, so a refused POST leaves every token row untouched (pinned on the table) and ADR-0043's single-use row ("consumed before deciding") still holds — nothing is decided on the refusal path. The `input!.comment as string` cast is sound: an empty issue list means the value is present and passed the `textarea` value schema. `actionRedemptionPage` is the single source of status and bytes; `handleActionPage` reads the last `comment` with `getAll`, matching the mount's parser. The refusal reveals nothing a GET with the same token does not already show.
- **`action-link-pages.ts` — holds.** Nothing the approver typed is echoed back (a refused reason is blank by definition), so there is no reflected input; token, act path and refusal copy all go through `esc`; the textarea starts empty. The approve form is byte-identical to before. The `required` attribute stops an empty submit in the browser; whitespace-only passes the browser and is refused by the server, as it should be.
- **`approvals-plugin.ts` — holds.** `body?.comment` from `parseBody` (last value of a repeated field; a file part is a non-string and is refused, as at the member). Same builder, same status.
- **`approval-service.test.ts` / `action-page-member.integration.test.ts` — hold.** The pins cover: typed reason recorded and no "Via action link" row; six blank shapes refused with all tokens unconsumed, request pending, no reject row, then the same link deciding; approve ignoring a sent `comment`; the page carrying the field; `400` with the exact refusal page; door parity incl. last-of-repeated `comment`. The three edited existing cases were strengthened, not weakened.
- **Break attempts.** Double-submit with a reason: the second answers "Already used" (unchanged behaviour). Blank reason on a dead link: dead page, `200`. Token action cannot be spoofed from the request. Very long reason: no cap here, bounded by the transport body limit, same as the `/reject` door; the column is a textarea. CSRF posture unchanged: the token is still the whole credential and no session is read. Audit row: actor, `acted_as` and attribution unchanged; the comment is the typed text, stored as sent (untrimmed), exactly as `decide()` stores it for the other doors.
- **Prose agreement.** `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx` matches the code (required field, blank answered the page again with `400`, link unused). The changeset matches except S1.

Findings:

- S1 (should-fix) — see ②. Prose-face fix; delta read owed.
- N1 (nit) — `IApprovalService.handleActionPage`'s docblock in `packages/spec/src/contracts/approval-service.ts` (outside the diff) says POST "reads the token from the `token` field" and "answers the result page"; the implementation now also reads `comment` and can answer the confirm page with `400`. ADR-0043's Non-goals still lists comment capture as not shipped. Neither is contradicted on a ⛔ line and both doors agree, but the contract text is now incomplete. Both are governed/spec surfaces outside this card's file surface: follow-up card, not this PR.
- N2 (nit) — `peekActionToken` and `resolveActionToken` are now typed as able to return `reason_required`, which only `redeemActionToken` produces. Accepted deviation, or narrow the types in a follow-up.
- N3 (nit) — the blank judge is `String.trim()`, so a reason made only of zero-width characters (U+200B, U+2060) passes. This is the shared rule in `packages/spec` that `decide()` already uses, outside the diff; follow-up at the rule if wanted.
- N4 (nit) — no pin drives the `400` page through the hosted wire door (dispatcher + hono over a socket, `packages/qa/http-conformance`); the generic Response pass-through is pinned elsewhere. The platform checklist (`docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/approvals.json`) has no clause for the reject reason on the link, and its step text still reads "redemption … (comment 'Via action link')" without saying approve-only. Follow-up card.
- N5 (nit) — a reject via the link no longer carries any "via action link" marker on its audit row (the approve still does). This is what the card asks for; recorded as an accepted consequence.

No must-fix. One should-fix (S1), prose face only.
